title: Visual Function Abnormalities in Strabismus and Amblyopia and Response to Therapy
official: Oculomotor Disorders: Experimental and Clinical Study
summary: Amblyopia and strabismus are characterized by a reduction in visual acuity, contrast sensitivity, grating acuity, vernier acuity, reading difficulties and binocular visual function deficits. Treated patients have residual visual function deficits. The purpose of the current study is to quantify various visual functions in amblyopic and strabismic participants at baseline, during and at the completion of treatment.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* History of amblyopia or presence of amblyogenic risk factors.

Exclusion Criteria:

* History of neurologic disorders
